title: After 40+ years of gaming, generative AI helped me develop and release my first video game!
author: Cytochrome-22
selftext:
**After 40+ years of gaming, I finally developed and released my first video game using generative AI!**

I've always dreamed of crafting my own video game, and generative AI tools enabled me to fulfill that dream.

After months of development using ChatGPT, Codex, and Suno, I released **Escape the Stink v1.0.0** on November 19, 2026!

*Escape the Stink* is a ludicrous action-survival game built exclusively for the Playdate handheld console, featuring procedurally generated dungeons, tenacious enemy pursuit, and frantic thumb-wrestling battles using the buttons and crank.

**Small screen. Big chin. Terrible smell.**

Development involved a phase-gate approach, extensive iteration, performance optimization, and rigorous testing on actual Playdate hardware. I learned an incredible amount about game development along the way.

This is a personal passion project, not a commercial venture, so the game is available for FREE with optional donations.

🎮 **Game, trailer, original soundtrack, and development summary:**

[https://cytochrome22.itch.io/escape-the-stink](https://cytochrome22.itch.io/escape-the-stink)

It was amazing bringing Chinman and Stinkyman to life, and I'm actively exploring ideas for future games.

I'd love to hear your feedback and learn about your own AI-assisted game development experiences!

Happy developing and happy escaping! 🎮💨

comments.author: Physical-Bite-3837
comments.body: ChatGPT is good at generating still images but sucks at animation and creating spritesheets. It can never do runs or walk cycles correctly for some reason but will do other types of animations with little problem. I’ll usually do the animations is seedance and then have ChatGPT covert them to spritesheets. Another probably with ChatGPT is consistency. If you ask for more than one sprite sheet for the same character often times it will slightly change the color, offset or thickness and height of the character and it’s often not immediately noticeable until you actually put it into a game engine for the animation.

replies.author: Cytochrome-22
replies.body: Excellent feedback, thank you! Yes, it was difficult wrestling with ChatGPT to generate consistent sprites.  I will look into seedance and other methods for generating reliable animation workflows.
